reader.requirement: At 85, at a successful OPEN the record delimiter in force must be the one the RECORD DELIMITER clause of the file control entry for the OPEN's file-name specifies; WiseOwl declines the clause, so the delimiter in force at every OPEN is the implementor's default method whatever the entry writes.

edition-consulted.switches: DELIMITER and STANDARD-1 reserved at all four editions

reader.edition-search: as for GR2; the OPEN path in SequentialConnector carries no delimiter setting and no edition input (grep for RecordDelimiter in the runtime IO directory: comments only).
reader.witnesses-cover: all of the rule's range at this edition: OPEN of files whose entries write STANDARD-1, an implementor-name and no clause

probes.printed: OPEN of F1 (STANDARD-1), F2 (VARREC), F3 (no clause) all succeed and read back as written; the three files are byte-identical; F4 (STANDARD-1, missing file) OPEN 35 then READ 47
probes.expected: the declined clause leaves the default method in force at every successful OPEN; a failed OPEN establishes nothing

probes.printed: COBOL1778 on each clause; A, B, C and D framed alike

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.2.8.4 GR5  (║2.8.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: GR5 binds the delimiter at OPEN to the clause of the entry associated with the OPEN's file-name; with the clause declined (docs/conformance/2/26.md, COBOL1778) every entry yields the one default method, so the rule's subject is the declined element. Verdict by the kb/Work PB5373 class-3 decision, the same as GR6; the witness is COBOL1778 at --std 85.
